text: Theoretically it works because you assume the pool of potential members is infinite. It isn't. For the payouts to continue, each person at every level has to recruit more people than the level above them. That means the base has to keep growing exponentially, which requires a doubling of members at every single tier. In a finite population, that growth becomes impossible very quickly. You can't recruit infinite people. The money from the new entrants just moves up the chain, which is a bit unfair to the bottom tiers. It works for a little while, and the people at the top do get rich, but the scheme eventually crashes because there simply aren't enough new people to plug into the bottom. You don't need a PhD in finance to see this, though the companies selling it always seem to forget the finite-population part. It's just a slower, more polite way of taking money.
